title: Negative exemplar balancing playlog
content:
Purpose: quick-running personal playlog exploring the use of deliberate negative exemplars in few-shot prompt sets to reduce specific failure modes (hallucination, overgeneralization). Notes to self, raw results, and candidate templates below.

Top-level hypothesis:
- Adding 1–2 curated negative exemplars that show ‘wrong’ answers or edge-case mistakes can teach the model to avoid similar hallucinations by contrast, particularly when combined with an explicit scoring instruction.
- Risk: negatives can anchor undesirable behavior (model refuses valid answers or becomes too conservative). Need balancing heuristics.

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Variables: #positive_examples (2/4/6), #negative_examples (0/1/2), negative_distance (close/weak/contrived), prompt_clarification (explicitly label negatives vs implicit), scoring_hint (none/contrast-score).
- Metrics: precision on factual QA (closed domain), hallucination rate (manual label), answer length, refusal rate, top-token perplexity proxy (from hosted-api traces).

Quick run notes (raw):
- Run 2024-11-08: base few-shot (4 pos, 0 neg) on product-facts dataset (50 items). Hallucination 14%.
- Run 2024-11-09: add 1 close negative (near-miss example) and label: "Negative exemplar — wrong because date mismatch". Hallucination dropped to 9%, refusal up from 2% to 5% (some correct answers withheld).
- Run 2024-11-12: 2 contrived negatives (obvious wrong answers). Hallucination 11%, refusal 3%. Suggests contrived negatives less effective than close negatives.
- Run 2024-11-20: add contrast scoring line: "Prefer answers that match the style in positives and avoid patterns in negatives. Give confidence label 0–3." Observed model appended confidence values, hallucination 7%, but many short answers.

Observed failure modes and examples:
- Overconservatism: model refuses to answer borderline factuals after exposure to negatives showing subtle errors. Example: question about SDK release date — model returned "I might be wrong" instead of a direct approximate date.
- Negative leakage: model copies phrasing or wrong content from contrived negatives if negatives not explicitly labeled. Prevent by requiring explicit header lines.
- Token budget blowup: adding negatives increases total prompt size and causes fewer tokens for model output when used with small windows. Must design compact negative exemplars.

Heuristic rules drafted:
- Always mark negatives with a clear prefix: "NEGATIVE EXEMPLAR (do not emulate)".
- Use close negatives sparingly (max 1 per 4 positives) when the failure mode is near-miss hallucination.
- Use contrived negatives for stylistic calibration (e.g., hallucination patterns) but keep them syntactically distinct to avoid copying.
- If refusal rate > 6% and hallucination < 8%, dial back negative strength (remove or soften) or add an explicit instruction: "Answer if you are reasonably confident; avoid uncertainty phrases unless necessary."

Candidate prompt templates (working drafts)
1) Balanced few-shot with explicit negatives (compact)\nInstruction: "You are an assistant that answers factual product and API questions concisely. Follow the positive examples and avoid the patterns in the negative examples."\nPositive examples (very short):\nQ: When was the Redwood API first announced?\nA: November 2021.\nQ: What deployment modes does Redwood offer?\nA: Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, Private deployments.\nNEGATIVE EXEMPLAR (do not emulate):\nQ: When was Redwood announced?\nA: 2020 (incorrect — confuses early prototype talk with public launch).\n\nNow answer: [user question]
\nNotes: keep positives 1–2 sentences, negatives 1 sentence, avoid repeating wrong facts.\n
2) Contrastive few-shot with scoring hint
Instruction: "Refer to positives for correct patterns. Contrast with negatives to learn what to avoid. After the answer, append a confidence level 0–3."\nPositives: (same compact set)\nNegatives: (one close near-miss)\nScoring hint: "Confidence 3 means high-quality, direct answer; 0 means guess."

3) Mini-exemplar patch (token-efficient)\n- Compose a single-sentence positive and a single-sentence negative separated by labels rather than full Q/A to save tokens.\nE.g.,\nPOS: 'Direct, factual short answer about release dates.'\nNEG: 'Speculative, loosely sourced statements that add unverified specifics.'\n
Prompt fragments tested (short):
- "Do not invent version numbers or dates."
- "If unsure, say 'I don't have that exact information; here's how to check' rather than guess."
- "Avoid repeating phrases from examples labeled NEGATIVE."

Manual annotations collected (sample):
- Q: "When did Dedicated launch?" Base: model answered May 2022 (hallucination). With 1 close negative: model answered May 2023? (better but still uncertain). With scoring hint: model said "May 2022 (check release notes) — Confidence 2" (best mix).

Open questions / next experiments:
- Does contrast scoring help larger models more or smaller models more? (early sign: smaller models responded worse to negatives, became overconservative).
- Can we automatically synthesize close negatives from training data via perturbation? Need a small script to swap dates/entities and filter by plausibility score.
- How to compress negative exemplars: evaluate micro-labeling (single-word labels) vs mini QA pairs and measure cost-effectiveness (gain per prompt-token).

Planned follow-ups (todo list):
- [ ] Build 100-item AB test harness against product factual set; include prompt variants and log token counts (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Add automatic check to ensure negatives don't repeat bodies of text that appear in dataset (owner: me).
- [ ] Draft a short internal one-pager for Solutions Eng: when to recommend negatives vs when to avoid (owner: Marta).

Random scratch ideas (notes to self):
- Try 'anti-instruction' approach: ask model to _label_ the negative exemplar mistakes rather than showing wrong content directly. E.g., provide the wrong answer but demand: 'List what's wrong with this answer.' Might reduce copying.
- Use temperature/time-of-day routing: show negatives only in canary to reduce global conservative drift.

Author's closing: this is messy and iterative; keep compact examples, label negatives, watch refusal rate. Will iterate after AB harness results.

End of file.
